verdicts.trueWording: Unlike much epic fantasy, he does not bury the reader
verdicts.note: Page, section 'Lyrical clarity rather than baroque fantasy': 'Unlike much epic fantasy, he does not bury the reader in invented terminology or ornate description.' Quote and both limbs (the contrast with epic fantasy, the no-burying claim) present verbatim. Raw HTML fetched via curl with browser UA, stripped to text.

verdicts.trueWording: The beauty of the prose comes from rhythm and precision
verdicts.note: Same section, verbatim: 'The beauty of the prose comes from rhythm and precision, not spectacle.' Whole claim supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay's sentences are musical, but they are rarely flashy
verdicts.note: Same section, opening sentence verbatim; 'musical' and 'rarely flashy' both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: People speak with restraint, implication, and subtext
verdicts.note: Section 'Dialogue as character and culture', verbatim; the surrounding sentences make 'People' Kay's characters ('His dialogue is formal... shaped by the social worlds his characters inhabit').

verdicts.trueWording: Triumphs are provisional. Victories are costly.
verdicts.note: Section 'Melancholy as a narrative tone', two consecutive sentences verbatim. Feature label 'consequence on a household' is a categorisation, not a claim limb.

verdicts.trueWording: his frequent use of memory, foreknowledge, and reflective distance
verdicts.note: Same section: 'Stylistically, this appears in his frequent use of memory, foreknowledge, and reflective distance' - 'this' refers to the quiet melancholy, so the stylistic-expression limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: the master of a specific type of omniscient tight third person
verdicts.note: Paragraph beginning 'Guy Gavriel Kay is the master of a specific type of omniscient tight third person narration'. Verbatim, page location as cited.

verdicts.trueWording: narrative commentary, foreshadowing, and emotional emphasis apart from the character's thoughts
verdicts.note: Same paragraph: 'the reader sees what a character is thinking but also gets narrative commentary, foreshadowing, and emotional emphasis apart from the character's thoughts.' 'separate from' = the page's 'apart from'.

verdicts.trueWording: if something is important, Kay tells you, explicitly and sometimes repetitively
verdicts.note: Same paragraph, verbatim (the quote's truncation continues '...repetitively'). The 'rather than leaving it to the reader' limb is carried by the same paragraph: 'It can feel heavy-handed' and 'The narrator will ensure that you don't miss anything important.'

verdicts.trueWording: The narrative commentary functions like a soundtrack in a movie
verdicts.note: Same paragraph, verbatim, immediately followed by 'It tells you when to pay close attention and when you can relax', which supports the attention limb.

verdicts.trueWording: just a moment of doubled perspective or retrospective commentary
verdicts.note: Paragraph beginning 'Kay also strikes just the right balance...': 'He will often switch viewpoint characters in the middle of a scene, but he avoids the trap of replaying the scene... There is instead just a moment of doubled perspective or retrospective commentary.' All three limbs present.

verdicts.trueWording: usually through the eyes or memory of the relevant characters
verdicts.note: Section 'World-Building & Exposition': 'Important circumstances are explained whenever needed, usually through the eyes or memory of the relevant characters.' Verbatim; the piece is about Tigana throughout.

verdicts.trueWording: a limited omniscience that vacillates between being in someone's head
verdicts.note: Section 'Writing Style': 'Instead Kay employs a limited omniscience that vacillates between being in someone's head and being more objective for certain scenes.' The 'standing more objectively outside it' limb is the page's 'being more objective for certain scenes'.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay changes narrative distance incredibly well, zooming in and out
verdicts.note: Same section, verbatim ('...zooming in and out of the narrative'); the detailed/sparse limb is the next sentence: 'A given scene may be very detailed or rather sparese [sic], but always for good reason'.

verdicts.trueWording: And frankly, some of his names are poor
verdicts.note: Section 'Why You Might Not Love It', verbatim; the examples given (Alberico the Barbadian, Brandin of Ygrath) are Kay's invented Tigana names, supporting the 'invented names in Tigana' limb.
